hitl_conditions: Human keeps setting inventory/cash policies; the twin's decision tree is chosen as white-box so decision-makers can understand rules; analysts filter rules by service level >=98% and pick the lowest-CCC rule. Not theorised as a change in role.
key_finding: Simulation-generated data trained a CART decision tree (83-86% accuracy) whose rules set inventory and cash replenishment policies; centralised planning with these rules cut the manufacturer's cash conversion cycle by 11.1 and 9.5 weeks versus decentralised planning, with and without disruptions; the wholesaler's ordering policy drives manufacturer CCC.

quotes.text: Therefore, in this study, we develop a SC digital twin framework that integrates simulation and machine learning. Figure 1 shows the developed SC digital twin framework.
Finally, the inventory and cash replenishment policies are outputted to the physical SC to inform decision making of the firms.
In this study, a single-product serial SC is considered. This is a three-echelon SC with one manufacturer, one wholesaler, and one retailer, see Figure 2. This represents a typical FMCG SC.

To obtain the cash management knowledge from the training dataset and structure it through a decision tree, we employ the CART algorithm in the Scikit-learn library. The 10-fold cross-validation method is used to validate the results.

The research seeks to provide guidelines to assist decision-makers in setting out inventory and cash replenishment policies by generating decision rules. This helps the decision-makers in understanding the decision making process.
